L41: Species: Dog
L42: 
L43: Area of Study: Medical Oncology
L44: Purpose of Study: The purpose of this study is to provide a direct comparison between the outcomes for dogs with peripheral T cell lymphoma (PTCL) treated with CHOP or LOPP chemotherapy. The findings of this study could help veterinarians understand if one protocol is truly superior to the other for dogs with PTCL.
L45: 
L46: In this study, your dog will be randomly selected to receive either CHOP or LOPP chemotherapy. At each visit, their lymph node size, blood work, and overall wellbeing will be assessed.
L47: Timeline: Both protocols involve treatments every 7–14 days and take 4-6 months to complete. Following protocol completion, your pet will return once monthly to assess remission status.
L48: 
L49: Eligibility: Your dog may qualify if:
L50:   * Confirmed peripheral T cell lymphoma diagnosis via cytology or histopathology
L51:     * No indolent forms of lymphoma, such as T zone lymphoma
L52:     * Cutaneous lymphoma will not be included
L53:   * No prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for lymphoma. It is preferred that patients are not started on steroids in advance of enrollment. However, if deemed by the overseeing clinician, patients can still be enrolled on steroids for up to 10 days.
L54:   * No major lab work abnormalities that prevent chemotherapy administration
L55:   * No evidence of dilated cardiomyopathy, ventricular arrhythmia, or liver failure
L56: ## T Cell Diagnostic Testing
L57: 
L58: A diagnosis of T cell lymphoma can be made using one or more of the following tests:
L59: 
L60:   * Immunocytochemistry (ICC)*
L61:   * Immunohistochemistry (IHC)*
L62:   * PCR for antigen receptor rearrangements (PARR)*
L63:   * Flow cytometry
L64: 
L65: *Available through the 【12†MSU Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory†vdl.msu.edu】
L66: 
L67: Client Benefits: This is a partially funded trial.
L68:   * A test must be conducted to confirm the T cell lymphoma diagnosis in study participants. T cell diagnostic testing can be conducted at MSU or through clients’ primary care veterinarians. Diagnostic testing at MSU costs approximately $250. For dogs accepted to the study, the cost will be reimbursed by an account credit at the MSU Veterinary Medical Center at trial completion (either when the protocol is completed or the patient develops progressive disease).
L69:   * Initial evaluation appointments will be charged. For dogs accepted to the study, recheck exams during clinical trial appointments will be free of cost ($60 value per visit). Costs associated with blood work and treatment will remain the responsibility of the client (with the exception described below).
L70:   * Dogs will receive the first dose of doxorubicin (for those assigned to the CHOP protocol) or lomustine (for those assigned to the LOPP protocol) free of cost. First-dose administrative and blood work fees also will be free of cost.
L71:   * Clients are financially responsible for all treatments and diagnostics that are unrelated to the study.
L72: Client Responsibilities:
L73:   * To administer prednisone, chemotherapy, or supplemental medications as prescribed by the attending veterinarian.
L74:   * To comply with the visit schedule outlined by study investigators
L75:   * To report any abnormal behavior or signs of illness to study investigators.
L76:   * To contact study investigators if your dog is evaluated by any other veterinarians during the course of the study.
L77:   * To inform study investigators of any non-study-related veterinary treatments recommended for your dog during the course of the study.
L78: Contact Information: Please feel free to contact our Medical Oncology Team at (517) 353-5420 or cvm.oncoinfo@msu.edu to refer a patient or for any additional information. Referring veterinarian and client calls are welcome.
L79: 
L80: Practitioners of interest: Primary care and specialty clinics, especially oncology specialties, in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, Canada, and surrounding areas.

L27: # Use of AI-enhanced patient-specific biomechanical modeling to identify dogs with appendicular osteosarcoma undergoing stereotactic body radiation therapy who would benefit from minimally-invasive intramedullary stabilization
L28: The aim of this study is to perform initial testing for stabilization of long bones affected by osteosarcoma using a minimally-invasive implant with FDA approval for use in humans.  A previous study performed by the OSU-VMC determined that this implant was safe and well-tolerated in dogs.
L29:  The current study uses artificial-intelligence (AI)-enhanced, patient-specific biomechanical modeling to identify dogs at higher risk of experiencing a fracture from their tumor and determines whether they would benefit from receiving the implant.  Ultimately, the idea is that this minimally-invasive technology could be used to prevent pathologic fractures for dogs who undergo stereotactic body radiation therapy for osteosarcoma.
L30: Each dog will receive a CT scan for radiation therapy planning, followed by 3 treatments of radiation therapy to the tumor.  The CT scan will also be used to assess the risk of fracture and determine whether the dog would benefit from placement of the implant.
L31:  If determined that the dog’s fracture risk would be improved by placement of the implant, following completion of radiation therapy, the dog will be placed under general anesthesia the day after the final radiation therapy treatment for implantation of the device.  Dogs enrolled in this trial will undergo chemotherapy treatment with carboplatin, an intravenous chemotherapy, for up to 6 treatments following completion of stereotactic body radiation therapy.
L32: Gait analysis will be performed at enrollment and at the 2 week recheck examination, followed by every 2 months, along with chest x-rays to monitor for spread of disease.
L33: 【8†Image: Older black and brown dog laying on a dog bed.】
L34: #### Client Compensation:
L35: The costs of the following will be covered as part of the study: pre-operative limb CT, pre-operative initial gait evaluation, anesthesia for implant placement, implant and implant application, intra-operative fluoroscopy, histopathology, and post-operative limb radiographs.  The study will also cover the cost of follow-up limb radiographs and gait evaluations.
L36:  In addition, at the conclusion of participation in the study, you will be provided with a $1000 direct payment to help cover other costs associated with treatment of the osteosarcoma.  This study does not cover the cost of stereotactic body radiation therapy or chemotherapy.
L37: ####
L38: Potential Medical Benefits:
L39: 
L40: Dogs participating in this study may avoid developing pathologic fractures of the limb affected with osteosarcoma.  The goal is to determine whether the AI-enhanced modeling and application of the implant to patients at risk of fracturing can prevent the development of fractures.
L41: #### Potential Medical Risks:
L42: There are some risks associated with anesthesia and surgery that will be explained by the primary clinician and detailed on the consent form for the procedure.  There are some risks associated with radiation therapy that will be explained by the primary clinician.  The risks associated with the implant include implant failure, infection, pathologic fracture, and tumor recurrence.  It is possible that dogs in this study may experience unexpected side effects resulting from anesthesia or surgery.
L43:  It is possible that the dog’s condition may not improve or may worsen.  The dogs will be observed closely for side effects and appropriate medical care will be provided.
L44: Diagnosis/Condition Being Studied: Osteosarcoma of the limb
L45: 
L46: Intervention to Be Studied: Minimally-invasive intramedullary implant following SBRT
L47: #### What qualifies my pet for enrollment?
L48: 
L49: Inclusion Criteria:
L50: 
L51: •    Radiographic suspicion for or cytologic/histopathologic diagnosis of osteosarcoma in the appendicular skeleton (limb)
L52: •    Intention to treat with stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT)
L53: •    Intention to treat with chemotherapy
L54: 
L55: Exclusion Criteria:
L56: •    Lack of cytologic diagnosis or radiographic suspicion for osteosarcoma
L57: •    Osteosarcoma not located within a limb
L58: •    Evidence of lung metastasis on chest x-rays
L59: •    Evidence of pathologic fracture at initial assessment
L60: 
L61: PRE-SCREENING QUESTIONNAIRE
L62: 
L63: If you believe your pet may be eligible for this trial, please complete a pre-screening questionnaire.
